title: Partial KV cache corruption reconstitution and retrospective
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:
This runbook captures operational steps, dashboards, and a post-incident retrospective template for handling partial KV cache corruption (a class of incidents where a subset of KV cache shards return invalid or inconsistent prefix state). It covers immediate mitigation, reconstitution steps, validation checks, and longer-term remediation and roadmap items. This document is intended for platform operators, on-call SREs, and platform product owners responsible for the LLM runtime cache layer.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to the distributed KV prefix cache used by the serving runtime (service: prefix-kv-cache).
- Focused on partial corruption scenarios: shard-level index corruption, checksum mismatches, or metadata-store drift that lead to incorrect cache keys/values but do not affect disk integrity globally.
- Not for full-storage failures, disk hardware replacement, or network partition incidents (see separate runbooks).

Why this matters (impact):
- Corrupted prefixes can silently degrade model quality (garbled continuations) or cause tokenization/decoding mismatches leading to client errors and elevated 5xx rates.
- Customer-facing symptoms: sudden spike in generation-quality regressions, small but systematic increase in perplexity on synthetic tests, and token-cost inflation due to frequent cache misses and re-priming.
- SLO impact: potential increased error-rate (objective: keep 5xx < 0.1% per region) and tail-latency pressure due to fallback warm-up paths.

Key contacts and ownership:
- Primary oncall: prefix-kv-cache-ops (alias: #prefix-kv-ops)
- Secondary: platform-operator-shift
- Owners: eng-platform / runtime caching guild
- Pager escalation: oncall -> tech-lead (within 15 minutes) -> eng-platform manager (30 minutes)

Signals & dashboards (what to watch):
- Dashboards to open immediately:
  - prefix-kv-cache:shard-health (showing per-shard checksum mismatch rate, republish lag)
  - runtime-generation:quality-regression-synth (synthetic prompts perplexity overlay by model variant)
  - token-cost:cache-hit-rates (per-tenant and per-region)
  - infra:per-shard-io-errors

- Critical alerts (recommended thresholds):
  - Alert: kv-cache-checksum-mismatch-high
    - Condition: > 0.5% of requests per shard returning checksum_mismatch for > 5m
    - Severity: p1
  - Alert: kv-cache-degraded-hit-rate
    - Condition: cache hit rate drop > 15% from baseline across > 2 shards for > 10m
    - Severity: p2
  - Alert: generation-quality-regression
    - Condition: synthetic eval perplexity increase > 8% sustained for 20m
    - Severity: p1

Immediate mitigation (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage and confirm scope:
   - Identify affected shards from prefix-kv-cache:shard-health and per-shard logs (tag: shard_id).
   - Determine if corruption is read-only (value mismatch, decoding errors) or metadata drift (index mapping incorrect).
2) Reduce customer impact quickly:
   - Enable degraded-mode for affected shards: route their traffic to warmfall shards or fallback path (see routing DSL: --route policy:prefetch:soft-fallback).
   - Apply rate-limiting for heavy tenants hitting affected shards if customer impact is concentrated.
3) Stabilize:
   - If checksum mismatches present, flip shard to read-only and quiesce writes for that shard (CLI: prefix-kvctl shard-set-mode --shard <id> --mode read-only).
   - If metadata-store drift suspected, scale down rebalancers that could be moving shards (prevent further churn).

Reconstitution procedure (detailed playbook):
Pre-reqs:
- Access: prefix-kv-ops SRE AWS/GCP project and k8s namespace prefix-kv
- Scripts and helpers: tools/prefix-kv/verify-shard-checksums.sh, tools/prefix-kv/rebuild-prefix-index.py
- Backstop snapshot location: s3://prefix-kv-backups/<region>/<date>/

Step A: Snapshot verification (10–20m)
1) For each affected shard_id run:
   ./tools/prefix-kv/verify-shard-checksums.sh --shard shard-42 --sample 1000 --out /tmp/checksums-shard-42.json
   - Expectation: if > 2% of samples mismatch checksums, mark shard as corrupted.
2) Cross-check metadata-store mapping:
   kubectl exec -it metadata-store-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -s http://localhost:8500/shard-mappings' > /tmp/shard-mappings.json
   - Validate that the physical shard matches logical mapping.

Step B: Choose reconstitution path (replay vs rebuild)
- If change-window < 2h and backups aligned: prefer replay from WAL (lower duration, higher fidelity).
- If inconsistent or repeated checksum failures: prefer rebuild (reconstruct index from authoritative source, slower but clean).

Step C: Replay from WAL (preferred when available)
1) Pause reads to the shard: prefix-kvctl shard-set-mode --shard shard-42 --mode paused
2) Load WAL segments from backup and replay in validation mode:
   prefix-kv-replay --shard shard-42 --wal s3://prefix-kv-backups/region/date/shard-42/wal/ --validate-only --out /tmp/replay-validate-42.json
3) If validate-only passes, perform live replay:
   prefix-kv-replay --shard shard-42 --wal <path> --apply --batch-size 10000
4) Run checksum verification again and compare to baseline.

Step D: Full rebuild (if replay not possible)
1) Quiesce writes and mark shard read-only.
2) Recreate index from authoritative source:
   python tools/prefix-kv/rebuild-prefix-index.py --shard shard-42 --source s3://model-prefix-authoritative/region/2026-01-30/ --out /tmp/new-index-42.tgz
3) Upload rebuilt index to shard node(s) and atomically swap:
   prefix-kvctl shard-replace-index --shard shard-42 --index /tmp/new-index-42.tgz --atomic
4) Run smoke tests (see Validation checks).

Validation checks (post-reconstitution):
- Run synthetic prompt test suite (subset): run ./tools/synth-eval/run-suite --suite prefetched-prefix-check --shard shard-42 --baseline <last-known-good>
- Compare token-level diffs for a random sample of 5k requests: token-diff rate should be < 0.5% for non-changing prompts.
- Recompute checksum histogram and ensure mismatch rate < 0.01%.

Rollback and customer communication:
- If reconstitution degrades client behavior, immediately flip shard back to previous index and open a rollback ticket.
- Notify support and customer success for any tenants that were throttled or experienced errors with a short incident summary and mitigation steps.

Runbook automation snippets:
- Example k8s job to run rebuild (YAML):
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    name: kv-rebuild-shard-42
  spec:
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: rebuild
          image: gcr.io/redwood/prefix-kv-tools:stable
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "python tools/prefix-kv/rebuild-prefix-index.py --shard shard-42 --source s3://... --out /tmp/index.tgz"]
        restartPolicy: Never

- Useful CLI: prefix-kvctl status --shard <id>, prefix-kvctl snapshot-list --shard <id>, prefix-kv-replay --dry-run

Retrospective template (to use after incident is closed):
1) Timeline: minute-by-minute timeline from first alert to final verification (include operator names).
2) Root-cause analysis: list hypotheses, evidence, and which hypothesis is accepted.
3) Detection gap: how long between the first symptom and the first meaningful alert?
4) Mitigation effectiveness: which mitigations reduced customer impact and how quickly?
5) Action items (owner & due date):
   - Add per-shard checksum guardrail: prefix-kv-safety (owner: runtime-caching, due: 2026-03-01)
   - Implement automatic shard self-quarantine when checksum mismatch > 1% for 10m (owner: infra-scheduling)
   - Add synthetic per-model prefix checks to regression dashboard (owner: ml-evals)
6) Postmortem writeup and communication checklist: internal summary, external CS note, legal/compliance review if necessary.

Longer-term mitigations and roadmap items:
- Short-term (0–3 months):
  - Safety guardrails: per-shard checksum alerting + auto-quarantine.
  - Snapshot/backup hygiene: verify WAL retention and alignment across regions.
- Mid-term (3–9 months):
  - Self-healing: operator-less rebuild workflow (automated Job + canary verification + staged swap).
  - Stronger invariants: store per-prefix CRCs and lightweight signature to detect silent bit-rot earlier.
- Strategic (9–18 months):
  - Move to multi-versioned index format that supports fast atomic rollbacks and namespace-level immutability.
  - Integrate reconstitution progress into Console with per-shard live telemetry and operator action buttons.

Retrospective example action item table:
- Action: Enable auto-quarantine on 3% checksum mismatch. Owner: eng-platform. Target date: 2026-03-15.
- Action: Add synthetic regression probes per region. Owner: ml-evals. Target date: 2026-02-28.
- Action: Harden rebuild job to use ephemeral nodes with GPU-affinity for speed. Owner: infra. Target date: 2026-05-01.

Runbook reviews and maintenance cadence:
- This runbook owner (runtime caching guild) should schedule a live tabletop at least once per quarter with platform operators and ML-evals to verify procedures and automation hooks.
- Update this runbook after any incident or quarterly if no incidents occur.

Appendix A — Example investigation commands and log queries:
- Check per-shard mismatch counts (datadog query):
  sum:prefix_kv.checksum_mismatch{shard_id:shard-42} by {shard_id}.rollup(sum, 60)
- Retrieve sample corrupted entries (k8s exec):
  kubectl exec -it prefix-kv-node-42 -- /bin/sh -c 'prefix-kv-tool dump --shard shard-42 --sample 200 > /tmp/sample.json'

Appendix B — Validation checklist (operator copy):
- [ ] Isolation: affected shard(s) routed to fallback
- [ ] Quiesced writes for corrupted shard(s)
- [ ] Reconstitution path selected (replay or rebuild)
- [ ] Checksum verification passed on sample
- [ ] Synthetic evals show < 0.5% token-diff
- [ ] Notifications sent to CS and SRE rotation

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Ava Patel (initial procedures and validation checks).
- 2026-02-03: Updated with replay vs rebuild decision flow and automation job YAML (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Singh).

Related pages and references:
- Cache shard reshuffle postmortem (see related_pages above)
- prefix-kv architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/prefix-kv-architecture (internal id: ARCH-PK-001)

If you have questions or suggested improvements, please ping #prefix-kv-ops in Slack or add comments to this page.
